data.turoyo: Ŭ šridi ʕam gabe, ŭ mčanqalle ad+dargat dlo+ʕəbri ... dlo+ʕobar li+walaye.
data.translation: And they followed by his side, and bolted the gates so they don’t enter … he doesn’t enter the city.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: plural gates and an overt purpose clause; spoken repair retained.

data.turoyo: Lu ʕamo di walaye d Xarpet ṣxərre at tarʕe qumayye, aš=šəbbake mčanqlənne, mayiṯi mi zuḥṯo d Ḥaǧi Badran Aġa.
data.translation: Die Einwohner von Charput verschlossen ihre Türen vor ihnen, hakten die Fenster zu und starben vor Angst vor Hadschi Badran Agha.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: overt windows resumed by a plural patient suffix.
The door is hooked shut, not hacked. The supplied translation at 56/139 reads 'Sie ist eingehakt', matching the sense 'einhaken'.

summary: The Kurdish hook-derived verb remains in glossary I, with its inherited base forms. The material supplies plural gate/window patients beside the existing singular door.

Active Preterit reports fastening; Detransitive Part. Pass. mčanqlo yo reports the resulting shut state. Repetition of the action in 56/138 remains two occurrence decisions but one already represented event.
mčanqlənne in 95/162 follows a topical plural window NP. The form belongs to the existing Preterit paradigm; no new stem or box is inferred from its suffix.
Confirm detailed segmentation of plural-agent/patient forms mčanqalle and mčanqlənne; the contextual sense and inherited stem allocation are secure.
Hook-fastening applies to gates and windows as well as a house door; no meaning change.
